sourceReceipts.title: AI Companies Still Haven't Delivered on Their Biggest Promises
sourceReceipts.notes: The complete edition Markdown and complete available transcript were read. AIDB argues that industry trust cannot be repaired by messaging alone and that even a major medical breakthrough would not settle questions about pricing, access, lobbying, opacity, distribution and power. This is preserved as attributed analysis; its named empirical and product claims were not independently reconstructed in this bounded archive pass.

sourceReceipts.title: The New Problems AI Is Creating (And How People Are Solving Them)
sourceReceipts.notes: The complete edition Markdown and complete available transcript were read. AIDB shifts the question from whether AI matters to how work should be redesigned, including value per unit of intelligence, anti-slop controls, workforce investment, de-skilling risk and owning the surrounding harness. Named EY, OpenAI, BCG, KPMG and Clay evidence was not independently reconstructed, so no factual or practice claim is admitted.

sourceReceipts.title: How to Decide What Work AI Should Do for You: The AI Deputization Audit
sourceReceipts.notes: The complete edition Markdown and complete available transcript were read. AIDB's five criteria—frequency and time, teachability, checkability, stakes and personal dependence—lead to deputize, duet or defend. The durable decision framework is useful, but named 2026 product capabilities and workflows are volatile and remain unverified; this is not a Paige tip until official evidence and a bounded task test pass.

sourceReceipts.title: SpaceXAI Adopts NVIDIA Vera CPU to Accelerate Agentic AI at Massive Scale
sourceReceipts.notes: NVIDIA's August 24 company release says SpaceXAI plans to deploy Vera CPUs and Rubin systems and describes CPU work coordinating tools, code and data between model calls. The release is authoritative only for NVIDIA's announcement and framing; deployment and performance are forward-looking and not independently established. The same event appeared in Rundown, TLDR AI and The Neuron and is normalized here once.

opportunities.title: Explain how AI changes the shape of work, not only the number of jobs
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can distinguish tasks, jobs and organizations, then see where judgment, responsibility and decision rights move when agents take on more work.
opportunities.facts: AIDB published August 16 and August 23 editions about redesigning work and the future of human-agent organizations; the complete editions and transcripts were accessible.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: Across the two editions, AIDB argues that the job-loss question is too blunt: organizations must redesign work around value, verification, workforce investment and the human capacities that should not be casually surrendered.
opportunities.laidiesInference: The August 16 episode strengthens the existing theme with de-skilling, measurement and organizational-design questions; it does not earn a duplicate article. LAiDIES should explain the task-to-system-to-decision chain and include unpaid work, worker power and distributional consequences.

opportunities.title: Teach agentic delegation through permissions, boundaries and review
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can understand why giving AI tools changes the job from writing a better prompt to deciding what to delegate, defining access, checking the result and owning the consequences.
opportunities.facts: Mollick's July 23 guide and AIDB's August 14 Deputization Audit both distinguish low-stakes assistance from agentic delegation; both complete sources were accessible.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: Mollick emphasizes permissions, blast radius and review. AIDB adds frequency, teachability, checkability, stakes and personal dependence, then classifies work as deputize, duet or defend.
opportunities.laidiesInference: The combined durable mechanism is valuable, but product rankings, plan prices, mode names and capability claims must be rebuilt from current official evidence. This is a decision framework, not a universal product recommendation.

opportunities.title: Explain why a spectacular AI benefit would not settle the trust question
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can separate whether AI delivers a benefit from who controls it, who can afford it, who bears the risk and who can challenge the terms.
opportunities.facts: AIDB published an August 17 long-form episode about AI-company promises and public trust; the complete edition and transcript were accessible.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: AIDB argues that trust cannot be repaired by messaging alone and that delivery matters, while also acknowledging that a breakthrough does not erase questions about access, price, opacity, lobbying, distribution or institutional power.
opportunities.laidiesInference: The strongest reader frame is not whether one promised breakthrough makes AI good or bad. It is how evidence of benefit interacts with governance, distribution and the public's ability to influence consequential systems.

opportunities.title: Track the infrastructure that lets agent systems coordinate tools and data
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can understand that an agent's usefulness depends on the surrounding system that moves data, calls tools and controls action—not only on the model's conversational ability.
opportunities.facts: NVIDIA announced on August 24 that SpaceXAI plans to deploy Vera CPUs and Rubin systems; the release describes CPU work coordinating tools, code and data between model calls.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: NVIDIA presents Vera as infrastructure for agentic workloads and makes named forward-looking performance and deployment claims.
opportunities.laidiesInference: The announcement is a useful mechanism clue for a future agents explainer, but one vendor announcement does not establish deployment results, general performance or a reader decision today.
